title: Language: Miracle and Tyranny
coreMove: Use language as a bridge, not a verdict: join event facts with present sensation, and let other symbolic routes speak when words close too soon.

exampleSpecs.audience: program directors after a mass-casualty response
exampleSpecs.stakes: Official recommendations can miss what survivors' bodies seek when words are too narrow.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the gap between expert talk-oriented advice and body-based treatment seeking.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A listener can either gather more story or help the caller stay present enough to tell it.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show attuned listening shifting the body before narrative continues.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Detached facts can look disciplined while leaving feeling and bodily state split off.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Pennebaker's finding to join event sequence with emotion.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A coherent account can mislead the room if the body is absent from the telling.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Correct praise for narrative polish by returning to present sensation.

exampleSpecs.audience: arts facilitators and trauma program volunteers
exampleSpecs.stakes: Speech can close too early, leaving movement, sound, or image to carry material safely.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use art, music, or movement as a real expressive channel when words narrow.

exampleSpecs.audience: analysts comparing recommendations with treatment use
exampleSpecs.stakes: A briefing can either defend the official list or show the unmet need beneath the data.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Compare official post-9/11 recommendations with actual survivor treatment seeking.
